newsitem.title: UK: Dlr ends down in Europe as US markets soften again.
newsitem.headline: Dlr ends down in Europe as US markets soften again.

text.p: The dollar closed lower after a lacklustre session here, undermined by renewed weakness in U.S. stocks and bonds after the release of robust economic data and a mark rebound after German exchange rate comments, traders said.

News of a 9.2 percent rise in U.S. November housing starts to 1.51 million - versus an expected 1.41 million - undermined U.S. asset markets, coming hot on the heels of news of a brisk 0.9 percent rise in industrial output on Monday.
"The dollar continues to be sensitive to the gyrations of U.S. asset markets," said a senior trader at a German bank. "It finds good support though on dips, so I'm not that worried."
At 1558 GMT the dollar was at 1.5450/60 marks and 113.71/81 yen compared with 1.552025 and 114.15/25 in late European trading on Monday.

The mark was boosted, meanwhile, by latest exchange rate comments in the Bundesbank's monthly report, indicating that the market can no longer expect the German central bank to actively pursue a policy of further mark weakness at current levels.

Klaus Baader, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said the most relevant point was that the report said 1995 mark appreciation had been fully corrected now and that exchange rates broadly reflect economic fundamentals.

Criticism about the European Union stability pact from Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing also buoyed the mark, traders said. Issing criticised the lack of "automaticity" of fines to be levied on countries running excessive budget deficits agreed at the Dublin summit last weekend.

The customary wait-and-see attitude ahead of the conclusion of today's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting also kept a lid on the dollar, even though most traders expected no change in U.S. interest rates to result from the meeting.
The dollar made a brief foray above 114 yen after a Japanese minister called for a slightly weaker yen.
Kabun Muto, director general of the Management and Co-ordination Agency, said he felt the yen should be slighty cheaper than at present to help private industry.
But the dollar lacked impetus to retest Monday's high at 114.25 yen. Selling of marks for yen late in the session helped push the dollar back below 114 yen.
Dealers also noted the dollar's repeated failure to break convincingly through 1.5575/85 marks, a resistance area that capped advances last week and capped the U.S. unit on Monday.
"It's unlikely the dollar will break out of the established ranges ahead of Christmas," the German bank trader said.
The dollar edged close to 1.55 marks after the Bank of France cut its key intervention rate to 3.15 percent from 3.20 percent before withdrawing again on U.S. asset market softness, traders said.
The French franc was a touch weaker at 3.3765/67 per mark from 3.3733/38 in late European trading on Monday.
The Swedish Riksbank also eased credit, cutting its repo rate by 25 basis points to 4.10 percent. The crown dipped to 4.4120/50 per mark from 4.4075/75 late on Monday.
